messages:
maria_g: Heads-up — after promoting Blink int8 to canary on dedicated (pool-3) we see a parse-failure delta on toolcall outputs. Sampling window 1h -> parse failure rate up from 0.6% to 2.9%.

maria_g: Quick metrics snapshot from kibana: 
- total toolcalls: 23.7k
- parse_failures: 686 (prev 142)
- top failing route: /v1/chat/invoke-tool (latency OK)
- median tokens per response: 92

maria_g: Example malformed response (from mirror ID 0x7f3b):
```
{"action": "open_file", "path": "/etc/hosts",}  <-- trailing comma
```

jon_w: ugh trailing comma. Is this only in array/object endings or also missing closing braces?

maria_g: Mostly trailing commas and occasional duplicated keys. Pattern seems concentrated when KV-prefix length > 512 and when streaming cut happened (client closed around token 85).

samir: Do we have tokenizer mismatch between reference and Blink's compiled tokenizer? Could be producing unexpected control chars.

lena_k: I checked a diff of tokenization for that prompt — the boundary tokens are identical up to 88 tokens, then Blink introduces a CRLF pair before the JSON chunk. That line-break sometimes becomes a 0x0B in the int8 runtime.

eva_r: Is this happening for FP16 or just int8?

maria_g: Quick A/B: FP16 baseline has 0.5% parse failures in same window. Int8 canary 2.9%. So appears quantization related.

samir: Could be numerical instability causing the model to emit slightly different punctuation (extra comma). PTQ recipe used per-layer clipping + group-wise scaling. We did one extra epoch of calibration for Blink — wondering if that nudged punctuation logits.

jon_w: Any chance the postprocessing sanitizer (jsonwrap / closing-brace-healer) didn't run on canary because of new routing? I remember we gate that stage for latency-critical paths.

maria_g: Good catch — the canary overlay used mirror pipeline: no postprocess step to keep raw outputs for diagnostics. So the live stream is unmodified, yes. We should still see parse failures in mirror logs though.

lena_k: I pulled ~200 failing traces, heuristics show 78% have a trailing comma, 12% missing final brace, 10% have duplicated keys like {"id": "x", "id": "x"}.

samir: Duplicated keys smell like streaming boundary re-emission or retry/merge bug. Could the KV cache replay during batching cause partial suffix duplication?

maria_g: We also saw these failures spike with batch size 8 on pool-3; batch size 1/2 has far fewer incidents. Suggests batching/kvcache interaction.

eva_r: Actionable plan?

maria_g: Proposal: 1) Pause further canary bump to 5% hold. 2) Enable jsonwrap postprocess for canary mirror (cheap). 3) Run focused fuzz harness: token-boundary-aware mutator with Blink int8 weights to reproduce trailing comma. 4) Collect 1k mirror outputs and run automated json-lint and diff vs FP16.

jon_w: +1 to jsonwrap. Also add a retry-with-rewrite: if parse fails, run a lightweight heuristic fixer (trim trailing commas, close braces) before counting as failure. We have that code in repo: git.redwood/infer/tools/json_healer (small python).

samir: I'll spin up a targeted run with batch sizes 1/4/8 and kv-prefix truncation toggled. ETA 2h for first signals.

lena_k: I'll export a sample set for product/ops to review; will include tokenizers and raw logits for 200 traces. Uploading to s3://redwood-infer/blink/onboard-debug/6255554321/ now.

ops-bot: Deploy notice: canary overlay change queued by maria_g — will require config toggle `postprocess.jsonwrap=true` on pool-3.

eva_r: If the heuristic fixer reduces failure to <0.8% we can keep int8 but add permanent postprocess and follow-up quant tuning. If not, rollback to FP16 and open a quantization regression ticket.

maria_g: Agreed. I'll hold any further traffic increases until Samir's run finishes. Will post results here. Thanks all :pray:
